text:
alice: Quick thread — ran a chaos-style prefill sim against the v2 canary this morning. TL;DR: deploy-time warmers cut cold-start latency but KV hit-rate didn’t move as expected.
marco: Can you paste the run command and the perf snapshot? :eyes:
alice: Ran `./tools/prefill --mode=chaos --seeded=yes --traffic=synthetic:10k` against canary-3. Collected traces + perf counters.
jen: Topline numbers?
alice: P50 latency down ~12%, P95 down ~18% when warmers active. But KV cache hit-rate stayed ~22% (baseline 18%). Not the jump we hoped for.
sasha: Huh. Were you using exact prompt keying or normalized keys? small whitespace/tokenization diffs can kill hits.
alice: Used current canonical keyer: `sha1(prefix + normalized_input)` where normalization is trim+lower. I suspect tokenization-level differences from the tokenizer update last week.
marco: Profiling dump (abridged):
```
kernel_select_miss_rate: 0.14
avg_batch_fill: 0.72
kv_hitrate_over_time: [0.21,0.22,0.22,0.22]
kv_lookup_latency_ms: 0.8
end_to_end_p95_ms: 180
```
jen: Kernel selection misses at 14% after quant change? That matches the regression ticket. Any correlation between kernel miss windows and prefill responses?
alice: I overlaid traces — warmers do their job (reduce model init), but when the request path hits a fallback kernel we incur extra L2 cache misses and slower KV lookups. The fallback also disables the micro-batched path intermittently.
sasha: So two orthogonal problems: (1) key fragmentation due to tokenizer / keyer mismatch, (2) runtime behavior change due to kernel selection causing batch churn.
marco: For (1) can we add a transient normalization layer in the warmers that emits a canonicalized prompt sample set? e.g., runed keys with both old/new tokenizer to measure overlap.
jen: I like a canary job that schedules warmers which prefill using both key variants and records hits. That would be a scheduled job, not only deploy-time. Helps detect silent regressions.
alice: Proposed experiment: 3 arms — A) deploy-time warmers (current), B) scheduled dual-key warmers (generate keys with old+new tokenizers), C) autoscale-triggered synthetic traffic (spike-driven warmers). Run each for 24h on canary and measure kv_hitrate, p95, kernel_miss.
sasha: Add a fourth: randomized prefix sampling to cover permutations that users exercise rarely. Might bump hit-rate.
marco: Implementation notes: we should push a small change to the warmers binary to accept `--key-modes=old,new,rand` and `--samples-per-prefix=5`. Keep opt-in for canary only.
jen: Also log a small hashed sample of the generated keys (not full PII). That will help us compute Jaccard overlap between modes.
alice: I already have a prototype script that emits the sample set and posts metrics to /metrics/prefill. Will open PR.
sasha: Remember to include `--respect-lease=true` so we don't evict live caches during autoscale. We want prefill that plays nice with steady load.
marco: Good call. For kernel churn, ops idea: add a micro-batch sticky flag per-lease so if a node flips to fallback kernel we keep existing batches homogeneous for N seconds to avoid interleaving. Could reduce batch churn.
jen: Can we simulate kernel flips in the chaos job? Use `deploy-bot` to intentionally toggle `kernel_selector.force_fallback=true` for short windows.
deploy-bot: runbook: toggled kernel_selector.force_fallback=true on canary-3 for 30s at 2148234580 UTC, reverted at 2148234610 UTC. See /ops/audit/2148234.
alice: When we injected kernel flips in the sim, batch fill dropped to 0.55 and p95 rose ~22%. So kernel stability is critical to warmers' effectiveness.
sasha: Ops/infra followups: ensure kernel selection telemetry is per-request and exported. Right now we only sample 1/1000. Increase to 1/100 for canary.
marco: Action list: 1) PR for warmers binary supporting key modes (alice). 2) Scheduled dual-key job + rand-prefix sampler (jen + alice). 3) Chaos toggles for kernel fallback to measure batch churn (marco + infra). 4) Increase kernel-selection sampling rate on canary (sasha). 5) Add micro-batch sticky flag prototype (eng-runtime).
jen: Add eval rubric: delta_kv_hitrate, delta_p95, kernel_miss_rate, avg_batch_fill. Target: kv_hitrate +10pp or p95 improvement >=10% for same cost.
alice: I'll open the PRs and a short notes doc with the experiment dashboard. Posting links when ready. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
marco: SGTM. If scheduled jobs prove better we may move to periodic rolling prefill for fleet.
sasha: small note — watch out for token-level normalization causing legal/privacy changes. Keep raw inputs out of logs. Hash only.
alice: Agreed. Hash+salt with env-kept salt.
jen: Great thread. Let's run the experiment next Monday.
alice: ✅
